newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NTT gathers Asian carriers in Multimedia Forum.
newsitem.headline: NTT gathers Asian carriers in Multimedia Forum.

text.p: Japanese telecommunications giant NTT, freed to pursue international business only this January, secured a firm foothold in Asia on Tuesday by bringing flagship telecom carriers into a multimedia project.

"The new forum will boost NTT's (Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp) presence in Asia and provide a platform to develop a new telecom alliance grouping Asian coutries," said Hiroyuki Iba, analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in Tokyo.
NTT and 17 Asian carriers and companies got together in Singapore on Tuesday to kick off the Asia Multimedia Forum.
The member countries will conduct experiments and share information on next-generation communications systems by connecting them with high-capacity communications lines.
The forum will also develop cross-border multimedia applications based on applications and technologies developed by NTT.

"If the countries in the region have the same (technical) standards, it will really connect countries and people together," said Lee Theng Kiat, president of Singapore Technologies Telemedia, one of the founding members of the forum.

Among others are Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, PT Indonesian Satellite Corp, PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia, Korea Telecom, Telekom Malaysia Bhd, Smart Communications of the Philippines, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd and the Telephone Organisation of Thailand.
The cross-border backbone networks would also be used by businesses in the region for access to the Internet on an experimental basis, NTT said.

An NTT official said developed countries in Asia, such as Singapore and Malaysia, wanted to exploit multimedia applications in the most efficient way, while other countries hoped to catch up by participating in the group.
"We set up the forum because member nations' interests met," said Takashi Togawa, director of the Asia Multimedia Forum Project, adding that the forum was open to any carriers and manufacturers.
Rivals to NTT, however, see the move as NTT's demonstration that it would take a decisive role in development of info-communications technology in the region.
"It's a step toward making NTT's technology a de facto standard in the world," said Eric Gan, analyst at Goldman Sachs (Japan).

An official at British Telecommunications Plc, which is openly courting NTT for partnership, said the new forum would develop into a telecom alliance that could compete with Concert, a joint venture between BT and MCI Inc of the United States, or others.

"NTT will eventually form a partnership with such global alliances," said the official, who asked not to be identified. "The Asia Multimedia Forum will provide NTT a strong edge in negotiations with the existing alliances."
